 Weekly Distractions: Pop culture whiplash edition
 Sidelines staff 
 • 
 November 2, 2026 
 Jesse Jones Weekly Distractions: Pop culture whiplash edition 
 This week, the pop culture world has been reeling from impactful losses, unexpected shutdowns and surprise announcements.
 Sir Patrick Stewart died Oct. 29, leaving fandoms like “X-Men” and “Star Trek” mourning. On top of that, AO3, a popular fanfiction site, is under maintenance for a month and ILLIT has dropped their first project without longtime member Moka. 
 On the less dreary side of pop culture, both Curry Barker and Harry Styles announced and quickly released videos inspired by their recent works.
 Although the entertainment world has been bringing shock to many fans — for better or for worse — the Distractions team is here to keep you up to date and informed on all the pop culture happenings this week. 
 AO3 shutdown brings the internet into an uproar 
 Archive of Our Own, also known as AO3, is a popular fanfiction website. Launched in 2009 as a non-commercial space for fans to read and upload stories, AO3 is home to tens of millions of fanworks across 82,900 fandoms and has become a primary source of fanfiction for millions of fans. 
 On Oct. 29, the official AO3 status update account on X announced that the website was experiencing a few maintenance issues that would cause the site to go down.  
 However, users were sent into a state of panic when later that day the site’s status update X account posted again, announcing that service restoration could take up to a month. This marks the longest time fans could possibly go without the website. AO3 admins claim to have detected a security incident that led to the website’s temporary shutdown. 
 AO3 has not made any further updates on the website’s restoration, leaving fans unsure of when they can resume reading and uploading their fanworks. Emily Fonseca 
 The director of ‘Obsession’ releases haunting new short film 
 Curry Barker, the man behind this year’s “Obsession,” announced a dropped short film “MAMA BEAR” this week. In it, a young man wakes up to a frantic friend, dozens of missed calls and strange, ominous happenings. 
 Barker continues trends he established in his first feature film, like shadowy, uncanny figures lurking in corners and hidden themes that require theorizing and analysis.  
 Within the film’s five minutes, several questions arise and very few answers are provided. The YouTube video already has thousands of comments filled with fans both picking apart the short feature and admiring its craftsmanship. 
 Whether Barker’s next release is his sophomore theatrical film, “Anything but Ghosts,” in May or another haunting, short experience like “MAMA BEAR” even sooner, he is sure to keep shocking viewers with his unique filmmaking and bold writing techniques. Jesse Jones 
 ‘Minimum Wage:’ A new comedy show with weak reception 
 “Minimum Wage” has received backlash since its premiere on Netflix.  
 The new show dropped on Oct. 26, with stars like Grace Reiter and guest appearances by Randell Park. It is based on a YouTube series by American High Shorts and follows seven teenagers working at a pizza shop called The Slice Club. Each episode focuses on the characters juggling school, life, work and hectic situations. 
 However, viewers have noticed the lack of diversity in the cast, with all seven main cast members being white.  
 Another criticism viewers had was the format. The new show is shot as a mockumentary. People have pointed out that the exaggerated acting doesn’t work with the format of the show, especially compared to previous mockumentaries like “Parks and Recreation” and “The Office.” Erick Martinez 
 Sir Patrick Stewart dies ahead of ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ release 
 The legendary stage and screen actor Sir Patrick Stewart died Oct. 29 in his Los Angeles home following a brief battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy body dementia. He was 86. 
 Stewart starred in various TV shows, feature films and video games, from Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” to Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” film franchises and Emperor Uriel Septim from the “Elder Scrolls” video game series.  
 Stewart is slated to appear in the upcoming Marvel film “Avengers: Doomsday,” in which he will reprise his role as Professor Xavier. Logan Bowman 
 Noah Kahan is going on a stadium tour 
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Noah Kahan (@noahkahanmusic) 
 This past week, Noah Kahan expanded his “The Last of the Bugs World Tour” for next year with 31 stadium shows across North America and Europe. 
 Noah Kahan had previously announced six U.K. and Ireland shows for July 2027. Then this week, he added 25 North American stops and five more European stops.  
 To announce the new stops on his upcoming tour, Noah Kahan released a bug-themed venue teaser. The teaser pictured 17 bugs with hangman-style blanks underneath allowing fans to speculate where he might be playing before the official announcement. 
 General tickets go on sale Nov. 12, and Noah Kahan will be performing in Nashville May 4, 2027, at Nissan Stadium. Karlie Lohr 
 ILLIT’s first release one member down stuns with energetic music video 
 South Korean girl group ILLIT returned with their new single, “You’re Under Arrest,” released Oct. 26. 
 The group also released an energetic music video for the song, featuring the four members playing detectives who find themselves in wacky situations from getting into a gaming tournament with children to starting a flash mob on the street. 
 This is the group’s first release without their member, Moka, who went on a temporary hiatus in June to focus on health and recovery. Taniya Bryant 
 Gracie Abrams soundtracks an unstable relationship with new single 
 Indie-pop artist Gracie Abrams released her new single, “Here You Come, There You Go,” on Oct. 30, introducing punk-rock and synth sounds to her pop stylings. 
 The song details the toxic emotional turmoil of being in an on-again, off-again relationship using grungy guitar, synth beats and devastating lyricism. 
 Gracie Abrams on Spotify 
 The song has gotten several mixed reviews on Reddit , with the studio version receiving pretty positive reactions, but the live version from SNL called “meh.” 
 “Here You Come, There You Go” is one of five new tracks on Abrams “Daughter from Hell (Deluxe),” releasing Nov. 20, 2026.  Tucker Young 
 Dominic Fike releases new album 
 Dominic Fike released his new album “HOW TO QUIT SMOKING” on Oct. 30, after a three-week delay.  
 “HOW TO QUIT SMOKING” is the pop star’s third album, and his first since 2023’s “Sunburn.” It is 15 tracks and 40 minutes long. The record has a decent number of features, including Grace Ives, Danny Brown and Tay-K. Yes, the same Tay-K who is currently serving an 80-year prison sentence. 
 Fike sings, raps and shreds on the guitar in his new project. Much like his past work, the artist does not shy away from his wild past on this record. William Holman 
 Harry Styles releases surprise ‘Coming Up Roses’ music video during tour  
 For his hauntingly romantic track, Harry Styles released the “Coming Up Roses” music video on Oct. 26.  
 This comes as a surprise to fans as Styles is currently on his “Together, Together” Global Residency Tour in Madison Square Garden.  
 As the eighth track off his fourth studio album, “Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally,” “Coming Up Roses” showcases themes of vulnerability and desire for hope within Styles’ lyrics. The track tells the love story of having a connection with someone you know won’t last forever.  
 Executed as a visual storyline, the music video shows Styles ballroom dancing with multiple characters on a small vintage dance floor. Throughout the video, Styles switches partners and eventually finds everyone else matched with their loving pair while he’s sitting alone.  
 The track’s intimate lyrics and enchanting violin perfectly compliment Styles’ message of exploring a relationship built on underlying self-doubts while the video tugs at the viewer’s heartstrings of wanting the doomed love to work out. Zoe Kuhn
